instructions:
Below is a draft essay. Revise it so that it reads as if a US grade 8 student wrote it in class for a timed writing test. Keep the position it argues and keep it at about 171 words. The file must contain only the revised essay.

A measurement tool scored the draft on how it carries feeling. For each measure below it gives the current value and a target. Revise the essay so that its measures move to the targets; the tool will score the result again.
- positive charge (hedons per 1,000 words): now 106.6, target 59.1. Counts positive words such as good, love, fun.
- negative charge (dolors per 1,000 words): now 12.0, target 10.4. Counts negative words such as bad, hate, problem.
- words that carry charge (% of words): now 31.0, target 17.8. Counts share of all words that carry any feeling.
- charge under a negation (% of charge): now 4.8, target 2.7. Counts feeling words placed under not, never or n't.
- charge after an intensifier such as 'very' (% of charge): now 0.0, target 1.0. Counts feeling words placed right after very, really or so.
- charge after a contrast word such as 'but' (% of charge): now 0.0, target 5.9. Counts feeling words placed after but or however in the same sentence.
- net charge of the last fifth minus the text's mean (per 1,000 words): now 42.7, target -4.8. Counts how much more positive the last fifth is than the essay as a whole; negative means a more downbeat ending.
- how unevenly charge is spread over sentences (1 = as if words were dealt at random): now 1.4, target 0.7. Counts above 1 means the feeling is bunched into some sentences while others are plain; below 1 means it is spread evenly.

Draft:

Dear Principal,

I am writing to ask you not to make community service a requirement for every student. I think service is valuable, and that is exactly why I would hate to see it turned into homework.

My friend Dana tutors second graders in reading every Thursday. She goes because she likes those kids, and they can tell. Now picture a student who is only there to get a form signed. He watches the clock, the child notices, and nobody gains much from the hour.

There is also the matter of time. Several of my classmates work after school to help their families pay bills. Others look after younger brothers and sisters until a parent gets home at seven. A required number of hours would land hardest on the students who already have the least room in their week.

Instead, please make it easier to volunteer. Post openings, give credit to those who take part, and invite groups to visit. Many of us will sign up by choice.

Sincerely,
A student
